items.title: Xiaomi's Factory-Ready Humanoids
points: Xiaomi's humanoid robots completed a full 8-hour autonomous shift in an EV factory, sorting car parts from bins into storage racks without human control.
The system demonstrated autonomous error correction—when mistakes occurred, the robots identified and fixed them independently.
All production tasks for that workstation were handled by the humanoids over the full shift duration.

items.title: Robotics Breakthroughs in Memory and Flexibility
points: MIT researchers built a system that flags uncertain object descriptions and compares images from different angles to correct a robot's memory with 92% accuracy on object identification.
This advance enables household and factory robots to follow instructions more reliably, from locating misplaced items to assembling machinery.
ETH Zurich built FlexiQuad, a drone with a flexible frame (chassis that bends on impact instead of breaking) that continues flying after collisions at speeds around 25 km/h.
Japanese startup MUSE's Armo robot and AGIBOT's humanoids are now stocking supermarket shelves and convenience stores, handling complex retail operations during 24-hour trials.

items.title: Waymo Pivots from Uber Exclusivity
points: Currently, Uber ride requests do not guarantee a driverless Waymo vehicle, creating customer confusion.
Starting January 2028, riders in Austin and Atlanta will be able to book directly through Waymo's own app for a more consistent experience.
Co-CEO Tekedra Mawakana cited customer demand for direct relationships with Waymo as the reason for ending the exclusive partnership.
